title: Design System: Juan Diego Flores — Deployed Systems Console

display.purpose: The hero name only, in the world's display face (Michroma in the console, Neuropol on glass). One per page.

headline.purpose: Ledger figures and timeline rail endpoints — numbers, not titles.

title.purpose: Heads set inside a section's own mechanic; never a standalone stacked title.

label.purpose: Mono uppercase keys: nav, spec keys, credential keys, contact keys. Floor is 12px.

shadows.name: dark-none
shadows.purpose: The dark theme casts no shadows at all; depth is tonal bands plus hairlines.

shadows.name: plate-lift
shadows.purpose: Light theme: the default raised glass plate.

shadows.name: plate-lift-deep
shadows.purpose: The closing contact panel — widest and most lifted object on the page.

shadows.name: plate-recessed
shadows.purpose: Credentials, cut into the surface. Casts no reflection.

shadows.name: control-gloss
shadows.purpose: The aqua lozenge control in the light theme.

shadows.name: nav-glass
shadows.purpose: Light-theme fixed nav panel once scrolled.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for entrances, hovers and reveals.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Symmetric curve for disclosures, so a collapse is not front-loaded.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Colour, border and transform state changes on controls.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: Panels, scrims, nav fade, underline sweeps, theme toggle knob.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity 0.7s / transform 0.7s from translateY(22px), children staggered 80ms
motion.purpose: Scroll reveal for sections and their children.

motion.name: hero-in
motion.purpose: Four-element hero entrance, no animation library.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global reduced-motion contract; canvases are not mounted at all.

components.name: Primary Button (dark world)
components.description: The site's main CTA: amber lozenge-free slab, label face in capitals, with a trailing arrow that steps right on hover.

components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em; padding: 0.85em 1.4em; font-family: Saira, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid #222836; background: transparent; color: #eceef3; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1), background 0.2s, border-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary { background: #ffb84d; color: #3a2a0e; border-color: #ffb84d; font-weight: 600; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #ffcf82; border-color: #ffcf82; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffb84d; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-arrow { width: 1.05em; height: 1.05em; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1); } .ds-btn:hover .ds-btn-arrow { transform: translateX(3px); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary action: hairline border on the page ground, bone type, accent border on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em; padding: 0.85em 1.4em; font-family: Saira, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #eceef3; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #222836; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1), border-color 0.2s, color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); border-color: rgba(255,184,77,0.32); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffb84d; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-ghost:active { opacity: 0.65; }

components.name: Aqua Button (light world)
components.description: The Frutiger control: rounded lozenge, water gradient, specular highlight pooling on the top half and stopping at the midline.
components.css: .ds-btn-aqua { position: relative; overflow: hidden; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em; padding: 0.85em 1.4em; font-family: Saira, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #fff; text-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgba(0,56,90,0.45); background: linear-gradient(180deg, #34c3ff 0%, #0093e0 48%, #0079bf 100%); border: 1px solid #0068a6; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.85), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,56,90,0.35), 0 3px 12px rgba(0,106,168,0.4); transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1), transform 0.2s; } .ds-btn-aqua::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 1px 1px auto 1px; height: 46%; border-radius: 999px 999px 40% 40% / 999px 999px 22px 22px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.72), rgba(255,255,255,0.16)); pointer-events: none; } .ds-btn-aqua:hover { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #4fcdff 0%, #00a1f2 48%, #0086cf 100%); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-aqua:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0079bf; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Mono uppercase link with an accent underline that scales in from the left; the current section keeps it drawn.

components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 2rem; } .ds-nav-link { position: relative; padding: 0.4em 0; font-family: Saira, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8rem; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #8b93a4; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-link::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; bottom: 0; width: 100%; height: 1px; background: #ffb84d; transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; transition: transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link[aria-current] { color: #eceef3; } .ds-nav-link:hover::after, .ds-nav-link[aria-current]::after { transform: scaleX(1); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffb84d; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Glass Plate (light world container)
components.description: The light theme's only container: raised wet glass with a specular edge and a wet reflection pooling below its lower edge.
components.html: Autonomous agents and full-stack systems, shipped into production banking environments.
components.css: .ds-plate { position: relative; padding: clamp(1.25rem, 2.4vw, 2.25rem); color: #06344f; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.86), rgba(255,255,255,0.66)); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.92); border-radius: 20px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.98), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.6), 0 6px 16px rgba(0,74,117,0.1); backdrop-filter: blur(8px) saturate(1.15); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(8px) saturate(1.15); } .ds-plate::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 4%; right: 4%; top: 100%; height: 34px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(255,255,255,0.92) 0%, rgba(226,244,255,0.55) 38%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 100%); mix-blend-mode: screen; filter: blur(3px); border-radius: 0 0 46% 46% / 0 0 100% 100%; pointer-events: none; } .ds-plate-body { margin: 0; font-family: 'Source Sans 3', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1.05rem; line-height: 1.6; }

components.css: .ds-ledger { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; text-align: left; color: #eceef3; font-family: Saira, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-ledger-row { border-bottom: 1px solid #191e29; } .ds-ledger-row > * { padding: 2.5rem 1.5rem 2.5rem 0; vertical-align: baseline; font-weight: 400; } .ds-ledger-figure { font-stretch: 120%; font-weight: 800; font-size: 3rem; line-height: 0.95; letter-spacing: -0.03em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; width: 26%; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-ledger-row-lead .ds-ledger-figure { color: #ffb84d; } .ds-ledger-what { font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 500; width: 30%; } .ds-ledger-where { font-family: Saira, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8rem; color: #8b93a4; line-height: 1.55; }

components.name: Availability Pulse
components.description: The live-status dot used in the hero strip and the contact panel: a solid dot with a ring expanding out of it. Green in both worlds; the light theme's one green object.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em; font-family: Saira, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8rem; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #c3c8d4; } .ds-pulse { position: relative; width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: #7fd88f; flex: 0 0 auto; } .ds-pulse::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -4px; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid #7fd88f; animation: dsPulse 2.4s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1) infinite; } @keyframes dsPulse { 0% { transform: scale(0.6); opacity: 0.9; } 100% { transform: scale(1.8); opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-pulse::after { animation: none; } }

components.name: Theme Toggle
components.description: A capsule whose knob slides between the two worlds it names; in the light theme the track becomes aqua and the knob a sky pearl.
components.css: .ds-themetoggle { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0; background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-themetoggle-track { position: relative; display: block; width: 46px; height: 25px; border-radius: 999px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #9fe0ff, #4fc4ff); border: 1px solid rgba(0,121,191,0.45); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.9), inset 0 -1px 2px rgba(0,74,117,0.25); transition: background 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1), border-color 0.4s; } .ds-themetoggle-knob { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 2px; width: 19px; height: 19px; border-radius: 50%; display: grid; place-items: center; color: #0079bf; background: radial-gradient(circle at 34% 28%, #ffffff, #e8f6ff 44%, #a9dcfb 100%); border: 1px solid rgba(0,121,191,0.45); box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(0,74,117,0.3); transform: translateY(-50%); transition: transform 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.8,0.2,1); } .ds-themetoggle[aria-checked='true'] .ds-themetoggle-knob { transform: translate(21px, -50%); } .ds-themetoggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0079bf; outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 999px; }

narrative.northStar: The Console and the Aquarium Window
narrative.overview:
One instrument, seen in two weathers. The dark world is a deployed-systems console: near-black ink, hairline rules, bone type, a single amber accent that appears once per section and never twice, and cyan held back for generative signal only. Nothing is decorated; everything is ruled, tabulated or bracketed, the way a system that is actually running reports itself. The one exception answers the aquarium's bubbles: once the hero is behind you, Matrix-style columns of code fall behind the page.

The light world is a committed Frutiger Aero aquarium window. A fixed sky layer with a low horizon sits behind the whole page, bubbles drift up through it, and the content rides on raised glass plates that each end in a wet reflection. It is not the dark layout inverted: it is the same content read through glass, with its own material logic, its own rounded geometry and its own accent role.

The two are held together by one rule of construction: every semantic token keeps its name across themes and only its value changes, so a single scoped stylesheet re-skins the entire surface without touching a component. Both themes are first-class; neither is the default, and the first visit follows the operating system.
keyCharacteristics: One accent per theme, spent sparingly: amber in the dark world, water blue in the light one.
Eight sections, eight distinct opening mechanics; no shared section head exists to regenerate a template from.

Fluid modular type ramp (ten steps) with a type system per world: Michroma and Saira in the console; on glass, Neuropol for single words and figures, Unbounded 300 for sentence heads and Source Sans 3 for text. No monospace anywhere.
Dark world: flat, hairline-ruled, no shadows. Light world: layered glass plates, specular edges, wet sheens.
Browser surfaces (scrollbar, caret, selection, tap highlight) are themed as part of the design, not left to the platform.
AA contrast holds in both themes; tap targets meet 44×44; reduced motion is honoured everywhere including the canvases.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each theme has exactly one accent token, and it is spent once per section. Two accent objects in one screen region means one of them is decoration.

rules.name: The Signal Reservation Rule
rules.body: Cyan belongs to the generative canvases and to nothing else. If a border, label or button reaches for it, the answer is the accent or a neutral.

rules.name: The Four Jobs Rule
rules.body: The light world is sky (ground), water (ink, depth, accent), grass (life) and glass (surfaces). There is no fifth colour and no warm colour anywhere in it.

rules.name: The Same Name, New Value Rule
rules.body: A theme changes values, never token names. A new component styles against the semantic token (--bone, --line, --amber) and is themed for free; a component that hardcodes a hex breaks the second world.

rules.name: The No Shared Head Rule
rules.body: The stack "small tag → huge title → small description" is banned outright, and there is deliberately no shared section-head class in the stylesheet to regenerate it from. A new section invents its own opening mechanic or it does not ship.

rules.name: The 12px Floor Rule
rules.body: --step--2 bottoms out at 12px. It carries every data label on the site, and smaller does not survive a phone screen outdoors. Nothing is shrunk below it to protect a desktop silhouette.

rules.name: The First Screen Rule
rules.body: The display steps (1 to 7) scale on --screen: min(1vw, 1.6vh), never on vw alone. They were tuned on a 1440x900 frame, and a real laptop is shorter than that once the browser and the taskbar take their share: Juan's 1366x768 laptop leaves about 1310x610. A screen shorter than 16:10 scales them by its height; a phone held upright is always narrower than that, so its sizes never move. The text steps (-2 to 0) read the width only, because a short screen is no reason to shrink what is read. The masthead is sized to the first screen, min(--step-7, 13.5vh), and the thesis is 0.28 of it. The test is the first screen: the name, the thesis, both buttons and the status strip fit whole at 1280x600, 1310x610, 1366x625 and 1486x690, in both themes and both languages. A phone on its side, under 480px tall, takes the phone masthead on one line.

rules.name: The Instrument Numerals Rule
rules.body: Anything read as data or compared down a column carries tabular figures (.tnum); anything that is a key rather than a sentence is set in the label face, with the case and tracking its world gives it.

rules.name: The Adapt-Never-Delete Rule
rules.body: When something costs too much on a phone, the cost is fixed where it is created — capped pixel ratios, bounded canvas heights, one type step down. Features are not withheld from small screens; the three generative canvases ship on every device, gated only on reduced motion.

rules.name: The Reachable Region Rule
rules.body: On phones, primary actions live at the bottom: the menu is a bottom sheet under the thumb, and the action bar rises into view once the hero is behind you.

rules.name: The Gloss Pools Rule
rules.body: Gloss collects where a surface ends — the top edge of a plate, the upper half of a control, the reflection under a panel — and stops there. It never coats a whole element or the page.

rules.name: The Differentiated Plate Rule
rules.body: Plates answer to the mechanic they hold, not to each other: the run-in gets a waterline along its top edge, the spec sheet is squared at the head and lifted only at the foot, the claims are a shallow slip of glass, credentials are recessed, the closing panel is the widest and most lifted. Uniform plates would turn eight mechanics back into one container.

rules.name: The Hairline Structure Rule
rules.body: In the dark world, structure is drawn with 1px rules and tonal bands. If a dark surface needs a shadow to be legible, its tonal placement is wrong.

dos: Do style every new component against semantic tokens (--bone, --line, --amber, --ink-2) so the light stylesheet themes it without a new rule.
Do give a new section its own opening mechanic, in its own class namespace.
Do spend the accent once per section: one accent figure, one accent node, one primary button.
Do set keys, years, counts and any column of compared numbers in the label face with tabular figures.
Do keep prose measures capped (66ch body, 46–48ch leads) and carry display hierarchy with face and size: the display faces have one weight and no width axis.
Do draw icons as SVG paths on the shared 16-unit grid at 1.25 stroke; Unicode arrows are not an icon system.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces — scrollbar, caret, selection, tap highlight, theme-color — as part of any new world.
Do validate at phone width and on touch before calling a change done, and neutralise any :hover that would stick after a tap.
donts: Don't build an eyebrow → huge title → small lead stack, and don't add a shared section-head class that would make one easy.
Don't put cyan on type, borders or controls; it belongs to the generative canvases.
Don't introduce a fifth colour or any warm colour into the light world.
Don't cast a shadow in the dark theme; separate surfaces with a hairline or a tonal step.
Don't coat a light-theme surface in gloss — pool it at the edge where the surface stops.
Don't give every light-theme plate the same radius and lift; the plate answers to its mechanic.
Don't set any label below 12px, or shrink type to protect a desktop composition.
Don't drop a feature to make it cheap on a phone; fix the cost where it is created.
Don't hardcode a hex in a component when a semantic token exists.
